paper.title: Chaotic diffusion in the Solar System

thesis: Long ensembles of secular and direct integrations estimate a small but non-zero probability of Mercury reaching destabilizing eccentricities, with general relativity materially changing the risk.

nodes.title: How stable is the Solar System over 5 Gyr?
nodes.body: Quantify the probability and mechanism of large planetary-orbit excursions over the remaining lifetime of the Sun.

nodes.title: Integrate a secular ensemble
nodes.body: Propagate more than one thousand nearby initial conditions with averaged secular equations for five billion years.

nodes.title: Mercury has a low-probability unstable tail
nodes.body: The ensemble assigns roughly one to two percent probability to Mercury's eccentricity exceeding 0.6 within five billion years.

nodes.title: Compare relativistic and Newtonian dynamics
nodes.body: Repeat the analysis without general-relativistic precession to isolate its stabilizing effect.

nodes.title: Removing GR increases excursions
nodes.body: Large Mercury eccentricities occur more frequently when relativistic precession is omitted.

nodes.title: A secular resonance drives the risk
nodes.body: A resonance involving Mercury and Jupiter provides the dynamical route to high eccentricity; relativistic precession shifts the system away from it.

nodes.title: Confirm with direct integrations
nodes.body: Integrate the full planetary equations from ten nearby initial conditions for three billion years.

nodes.title: Two direct runs exceed 0.8
nodes.body: Two trajectories reached Mercury eccentricity above 0.8 in less than 1.3 and 2.8 billion years respectively.

nodes.title: Present architecture is not certainly stable
nodes.body: The current planetary configuration admits rare chaotic trajectories capable of producing very large Mercury eccentricity.
nodes.locator: Synthesis of secular and direct integrations

openQuestions: The ensemble quantifies sensitivity under the selected dynamical model; it is not a deterministic forecast of a specific future trajectory.
